title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 109
paragraphs: This being the case, the tyrants of Cyprus called together the commanders of the Ionians and said: “Ionians, we of Cyprus give you a choice: which enemy would you rather fight, the Persians or the Phoenicians? If you would rather array yourselves on land and try yourselves against the Persians in battle, it is time for you to disembark from your ships and draw up on land, and for us to embark in your ships to fight the Phoenicians. But if, on the other hand, you would rather try yourselves against the Phoenicians—whichever of these two you choose, you must try to ensure, so far as it rests with you, that both Ionia and Cyprus shall be free.” To this the Ionians replied: “We were sent out by the common authority of the Ionians to guard the sea, and not to hand our ships over to the Cyprians and fight on land ourselves against the Persians. We therefore will try to do good service in the post to which we were assigned; and you must call to mind all the evils you suffered from the Medes when you were their slaves, and prove yourselves brave men.”
